memo.verdict: Neutral; park; conviction medium at Triaging depth. The record parks thyssenkrupp nucera (NCH2-DE) because the modal return at EUR 8.50 is about 10.5 percent a year over eighteen months and 14.2 percent over three years against the 20 percent bar, the change the case needs (green hydrogen orders converting into revenue and margin) has not begun on the outputs, and the park rule applies on two gates: 'Transmission' (RA 8, E 2, BB 4) D and 'Leading indicators' (RA 7, E 2, BB 4) D; 'No mediocre management' (RA 3, E 1, BB 4) C and 'Business' (E 2, BB 2) C do not park it, and the record does not argue against the park. Progress triggers: a price at or below EUR 7.50; or a firm green hydrogen order of 500 MW or more from the European pipeline or an Indian tender; or a FY2026/27 guide for positive group EBIT on 16 December 2026 together with first hydrogen at NEOM and no new provision. Invalidate triggers: a further remediation charge of EUR 20 million or more; or no firm green hydrogen order of 200 MW or more by the end of 2027.
case: - Thesis: a bounded-downside option on green hydrogen orders, not a growth case. A profitable, cash-rich chlor-alkali core worth about the share price on the sell-side's arithmetic (cash-plus-core floor EUR 8.90 to EUR 9.50) carries a loss-making electrolyser business that the market values at the present value of its next two to three years of losses and nothing beyond (enterprise value EUR 455 million is 7.8x the core's FY2024/25 EBIT of EUR 58 million; at the sell-side's 10x EBIT the core is EUR 580 million, leaving green hydrogen at about EUR -125 million).

- The change the case needs is external and has not begun: customers must convert paid engineering studies into firm orders. Final investment decisions slip by several quarters; below 7 percent of green hydrogen projects reach one; 10 to 15 percent of announced European projects convert; 12 percent of 2030 projects have offtake, 1 percent binding; the IEA pipeline shrank 10 million tonnes and 75 percent of it (240 GW) is unlikely to operate by 2030. Order intake was EUR 3 million in the quarter to June 2026; one conversion (Moeve, 300 MW) since early 2026 against management's "weeks to months" since early 2026.

- The internal change is real, defensive and in the numbers: a new CFO and CTO; a strategy pivot from a 5 GW capacity target to the 20 MW scalum module, a 120 MW plug-and-play system, a lifecycle service portfolio (first eight-year, about EUR 12 million, Moeve agreement), a Portugal cell-assembly hub (EUR 10 million to EUR 14 million, lease 6 October 2026, operations 2028) and the BHEL collaboration in India; the SOEC exit (EUR 30 million impairment; up to EUR 10 million a year of EBIT and about EUR 20 million of cash from FY2026/27; avoids a three-digit-million-euro commitment); a cost programme of over EUR 75 million (EUR 25 million in FY2026/27, over EUR 50 million structural thereafter); operating expenses EUR 24 million in the quarter to March 2026 against EUR 28.5 million expected. Guidance cut three times (May 2024, March 2026, August 2026).
counter_case: - At Building Block 1, the strongest case against: the pipeline is a false friend and the floor is a value trap that costs EUR 0.40 a share a year to hold. The 1.9 GW of paid studies and the 14 GW active pipeline are not demand but a study-to-order gap that widens as developers complete engineering and postpone equipment; management has said conversions were "weeks to months" away since early 2026 and one order has come. The two mega-projects that made the revenue, Saudi Arabia (EUR 277 million) and Sweden (EUR 189 million of FY2024/25 sales), are finishing; the backlog covers a third of forecast sales; green hydrogen orders were EUR 3 million last quarter. The sector's base rate for distress is set (McPhy liquidated; Nel's impairments), and Chinese pricing 20 to 40 percent below Western equivalents deflates the margin any conversion would earn. The cash that is the floor is spent at EUR 50 million to EUR 70 million a year while the parent, which controls the general partner and has pledged its stake, decides what the cash is for. The shares drift to the cash-plus-core value at a trough multiple, EUR 7 to EUR 8, and stay there for years; the risk research puts the downside at EUR 7.60 to EUR 7.80; the sell-side's "option for free" is a value trap.

- Conceded in full: the hypothesis had zero hard inconsistencies against twelve months of data in the risk research and the bull profile seven; the outputs agree with it, not with the record; the conversion base rates are its evidence; the governance means minorities cannot force a buyback or a sale; the record's own modal return is below the bar, which is the hypothesis in a milder form.
triggers: - Study-to-order conversion (Key Driver): will the 1.7 GW European engineering pipeline convert within twelve to eighteen months? Possible, not probable: about even odds of one further order of 200 MW or more by the end of 2027; about 30 percent of a gigawatt (national RED III frameworks bankable, about 60 percent, times financed decisions in the window, about 50 percent, near-independent). Alarm: the "late 2026" award slips past the 16 December 2026 results with no order of 200 MW or more. Invalidate: no firm green hydrogen order of 200 MW or more by the end of 2027. Progress: a firm order of 500 MW or more from the European pipeline or an Indian tender under the BHEL agreement before the June 2027 results.

- Flagship commissioning (Key Driver): will NEOM, Stegra and Shell Rotterdam commission without further remediation charges? Probable, about 65 percent (NEOM over 90 percent complete, 110 modules handed over; upgrades made before commissioning; a clean quarter to June 2026); against it the undisclosed root cause, diaphragm robustness questions, Stegra's capital need. Alarm: any new provision or warranty charge at the 16 December 2026 results. Invalidate: a further remediation charge of EUR 20 million or more. First hydrogen at NEOM by the end of 2026 with no new provision raises the odds on conversion too.

- Cost programme and SOEC exit (Key Driver): break-even in FY2026/27 possible (about 45 percent); the EUR 25 million quick savings and EUR 10 million SOEC saving probable (about 75 percent each); the EUR 50 million structural tranche plausible (about 55 percent, needs a supply-chain reorganisation); a 10 percent EBITDA margin by FY2029/30 needs green hydrogen revenue of about EUR 450 million, the same condition as conversion. Alarm: a FY2026/27 guide for a group EBIT loss. Progress: a FY2026/27 guide for positive group EBIT on 16 December 2026 together with first hydrogen at NEOM and no new provision.

- The floor (Key Risk, cash burn): plausible but eroding; cover EUR 9.14 at 13x on the core plus cash, EUR 6.79 at the lowest peer multiple; falls EUR 0.40 a share per EUR 50 million of losses; consensus EUR 69.5 million of negative free cash flow over two years; cash trough about EUR 560 million at September 2027. Alarm: net cash below EUR 560 million before September 2027. Either direction changes the view: a buyback, or a parent decision to sell down.

- The multiple (Key Risk): odds that the 24-month-forward multiple is above 30x at eighteen months about 30 percent (the cleared branch); 26x or above about 55 percent; the uncleared branch 22x. Changes the view: a sector re-rating on a policy event (RED IV withdrawn; a European Hydrogen Bank fourth auction several times the third).
- Chinese price deflation (Key Risk): alarm, AWE gross margin below 10 percent (Redburn's bear mechanism); deep European penetration five to ten years away.
